text:
Date: 25th July 2026
To whom it may concern,
I understand Agnieszka Marsh wishes to apply for legal aid for a family dispute as a victim of domestic abuse. I have been asked to provide this letter in accordance with regulation 33 and Schedule 1 of the Civil Legal Aid (Procedure) Regulations 2012 (as amended).
I can confirm that our organisation is situated in England and Wales and has been operating for an uninterrupted period of six months or more.
I can confirm that we have provided Ms Marsh with support in relation to their needs as a victim, or person at risk, of domestic abuse.
In my reasonable professional judgement Ms Marsh was a victim, or a person at risk, of domestic abuse.
The matters I have relied upon to support that judgement are: Agnieszka told me Ryan called her worthless, belittled her in front of the children and blamed her for the abuse. Agnieszka disclosed that Ryan threatened to kill her if she left, and on one occasion put his hands around her neck. Agnieszka fled the home with the children and was referred to us by the police. Agnieszka described Ryan controlling all of the household money and giving her a small weekly allowance that she had to account for. After separation Ryan turned up uninvited at her workplace and sent over 84 messages in a week, some threatening.
We have provided Ms Marsh with the following support: emotional support, risk assessment, referral to a children's worker, help to apply for a non-molestation order.
Agnieszka Marsh needed this support because she was identified as a victim of domestic abuse and needed help to stay safe.
Yours sincerely
Tanya Hussain
Domestic Abuse Support Worker
Calderwick Women's Aid
